_readme: MEETING REVIEW — THE PLATFORM'S OBSERVATION POINTS, per meeting scenario.
What an advisor is checked on in a meeting of each kind. The mentor authors these;
a firm inherits them and may edit, switch off, or add its own beside them. Design:
design/features/meeting-review.md §3 ('Where the observation points are edited'), and
the approved drawing design/mockups/meeting-review.html Stage A.
🔴 THE ELEVEN TYPES BELOW ARE A SUGGESTION, NOT MIKE'S LIST. They were picked from
data/logic_trees.json by the session that drafted the design on 2026-09-01, under a
rule (the old P12) that nobody had asked for. His words on being shown it, 2026-09-02:
'i have ZERO idea where the meeting types being linked to logic trees came from'. He
has since ruled that meeting types are AUTHORED and CASCADE — mentor down to the
business entity — so these are to keep, rename or replace, and the ids here are still
tree ids only because that is where they came from and nothing has replaced them yet.
TODAY the id must still resolve to a tree, because that is where the NAME an advisor
reads comes from and tests/unit/meetingObservations.test.js fails the build on an id
that does not. ⚠ That is a CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL awaiting the authored-types
build, never a principle — no report, prompt or recorder walks a coaching tree from a
meeting type, which was checked across every use of scenarioId on 2026-09-02.
TWO VOICES PER POINT, AND BOTH ARE IN THE APPROVED DRAWING. `text` is how the FIRM
states the point on the manager's screen ('The meeting was framed…'); `advisorText` is
how the ADVISOR reads the same point on their own pre-set and coaching notes ('I framed
the meeting…'). Stage A and Stage B1 of the mockup show the same four points in those
two voices, so they are stored rather than derived — no rule turns one into the other.
`advisorText` is OPTIONAL: a point added by a manager carries one form and the advisor
sees it verbatim, which is honest rather than guessing at a first-person rewrite.
IDS ARE IDENTITY. `mo-` marks a point shipped by the platform. A point ADDED at a tier
is minted under that tier's own prefix (mm- mentor, xm- global, gm- group, fm- firm) —
see server/utils/meetingObservations.js for why sibling id systems must not collide.
Never renumber or reuse one: every decline and every override is keyed to it.
ONLY ONE SCENARIO SHIPS WITH POINTS, DELIBERATELY. `eoy_meeting`'s four are the ones
Mike approved in the drawing, character for character. The other ten meeting scenarios
are REGISTERED AND EMPTY — writing points for them would be inventing advisory content
nobody asked for (CLAUDE.md: wording is asked for, never assumed). The mentor authors
them on screen, which is what the hub-page rule exists to make possible.

points.text: The meeting was framed — what we would cover and why, in the first two minutes.
points.advisorText: I framed the meeting — said what we would cover and why, in the first two minutes.

points.text: A metaphor or analogy was used to explain a financial idea.
points.advisorText: I used a metaphor or an analogy to explain a financial idea.

points.text: Understanding was checked before moving on from the figures.
points.advisorText: I checked understanding before moving on from the figures.

points.text: Named actions were agreed, with an owner and a date, before the time ran out.
points.advisorText: We agreed named actions, with an owner and a date, before the time ran out.
